resolved_codes.summary: Label model 3 (flammable liquids): flame, black or white.
Gasoline, motor spirit and petrol for spark-ignition engines go under this entry whatever their volatility.
Petrol with a 50 °C vapour pressure up to 150 kPa (1.50 bar) in some climates is still treated as not exceeding 110 kPa (1.10 bar).
Tank-vehicles and demountable tanks for this substance may carry additive devices under set construction, approval, use, test and document rules.
General packing instruction for liquids: combination, single, composite packagings and pressure receptacles, with capacity/mass limits by packing group.
Liquids under IBC02 may use metal (31A/31B/31N), rigid plastics (31H1/31H2) or composite 31HZ1 IBCs, with B and BB limits per UN number.
R001 permits light gauge metal packagings 0A1 and 0A2 up to 40 l / 50 kg for packing groups II and III; packing group I is not allowed.
RID/ADR only: UN 1203 may use IBCs only if its actual vapour pressure stays within 110 kPa (50 °C) or 130 kPa (55 °C).
Up to 5 litres per inner packaging may be mixed with goods of other codes or classes that permit it, or with non-ADR goods.
Portable tank, Class 1 and 3–9: test 2.65 bar; shell See 6.7.2.4.2; relief Normal; bottom openings See 6.7.2.6.3.
Portable tank must not be filled beyond the degree of filling set by 4.2.1.9.2 (the 97-based formula).
ADR tank code for Classes 1 and 3–9: liquid tank, G (general minimum), openings B, valves/devices F.
UN 1203 petrol with vapour pressure at 50 °C above 110 kPa and up to 150 kPa may also use tanks designed to 6.8.2.1.14 (a) with 6.8.2.2.6 equipment.
Vehicle for flammable liquids (flash point ≤ 60 °C), flammable gases or UN 2015 > 60 % in tanks above set sizes.
Transport category 2: at most 333 per transport unit under 1.1.3.6 on its own; counts ×3 toward the 1,000-point limit.
Tanks: Prohibited in D, E (bulk or tanks). Other carriage: Prohibited in E.
Flammable liquids/gases: no ordinary portable lights in closed load compartments; FL heaters off during loading; earth FL vehicles before filling.
Chapter 8.4 supervision applies above 10 000 kg in packages, or above 3 000 litres in tanks.
Hazard identification number 33 on the orange plate: highly flammable liquid (flash-point below 23 °C).

result.caveat: The EU ICS2 stop-words list is non-exhaustive and updated periodically. A "clean" result means no listed stop-word was found — it does NOT mean the entry summary declaration will be accepted; your goods description must still be specific enough for customs to identify the product.
result.disclaimer: Reference check only. This flags terms from the official EU ICS2 stop-words list, which is non-exhaustive and updated periodically. A flagged term will likely cause an ENS rejection; a clean result does NOT guarantee acceptance — your goods description must still be specific enough to identify the product. This is not an ENS filing, not a customs-compliance determination, and not legal advice. Verify against the current official ICS2 requirements; for filing, use your customs broker or filer.
